U.S. Sanctions Eight Canadian Crypto Firms Over Iran-Linked Transactions The U.S. Treasury sanctioned eight Canada-based money services businesses on November 6, including NIA Nations, Million Exchange, Amin Exchange and Farah Exchange, saying they facilitated cross-border transactions involving Iran through digital assets. Treasury said several of the firms transacted with sanctioned Iranian crypto exchanges or addresses linked to the IRGC, while some also helped launder drug proceeds for Canadian trafficker Ryan Wedding by converting cash into digital assets and sending the funds abroad. Blockchain investigator ZachXBT said he had publicly called for sanctions against Iran-linked OTC brokers in Canada five months earlier. — link

Vitalik: Slowing the Hyperscale Expansion of AI Compute May Do More Good Than Harm Vitalik Buterin said he disagrees with the strong negative reaction to the anti-data-center movement, arguing that continued gains in algorithmic efficiency could allow AI capabilities requiring much larger data centers in two years to be achieved within roughly four years using existing infrastructure. He said slowing compute expansion could give society more time to address cybersecurity, biosecurity and other risks, while scientific progress is constrained by factors beyond AI, meaning a one-year slowdown in AI would not necessarily translate into an equal delay in research. — link

Vitalik: ETH Should Focus on Store of Value, Not Fee Burning Vitalik Buterin said Ethereum should focus more on ETH as a store of value rather than as a “fee-burning token,” arguing that fee burn was never as strong a valuation floor as it appeared and that maximizing fees could conflict with decentralization and capture resistance. He said Ethereum’s strongest attributes are decentralization and “CROPS” — censorship and capture resistance, open source, privacy and security — and that these qualities are better aligned with ETH’s role as a store of value. Buterin added that Ethereum should not be concerned even if fee burn remains below 10% of breakeven over the long term, saying ETH’s value can come from elsewhere. — link
